title: Shadowmaster
canon: Los Angeles, present day, one step past now (setting ruled by Marco 2026-07-13). Elite gamers, the Shadow Masters, command real human avatars through concealed earpieces and body-cams in high-stakes staged scenarios: underground poker, urban war games, an Old West shootout. The avatars are people, not pixels, held by debts and contracts, and they can defy the voice, pitting strategy against free will. NRC feature first; (310) co-production because it is set in LA.
look: Cold neon and warm panic: beautiful interfaces, ugly rooms. Two cities stacked, the chair and the board: control hubs are climate-controlled, elevated and server-cooled blue; street level is sodium vapor, sun-bleach and dying fluorescent. Never postcard LA, always the working city: card parlours, container yards, backlots, parking structures. The signature cut is the Operator's mouth moving and a stranger across the city doing the thing.
note: Two treatments read: shadow-masters-treatment-v2.pdf (04-documents) and the earlier artifacts/treatment.html. Chose the v2 scripted treatment because canon adopted its engine and scenarios almost verbatim (the 00 Project logline: underground poker / urban war games / Old West shootouts, avatars may defy), and its three scenario worlds give concrete iconic frames, where the earlier treatment is a format-philosophy page with almost no photographable material. One correction applied: v2 places scenes in Brooklyn and Philadelphia, but Marco ruled the setting is Los Angeles (2026-07-13), so every shot is relocated to LA. Cast-continuity warnings: no cast is established, so no face refs are attached anywhere; do NOT reuse 08-shadowmaster-01-boy-avatar.jpg as a ref, its teenage controller contradicts the adult Operator shape and it carries letterbox bars. Racks_Data_Center.jpg is the only real photograph and carries server-infrastructure texture only. Separately pending for Marco: the two writers-room feature treatments (Opus/Wren vs Sol/Eli) still need his spine pick; this spec draws from the approved pitch-treatment layer, not those. — 2026-07-16: six story shots appended under the Story Law and Marco's Nova ruling. The anonymous Operator is superseded as the story's engine by NOVA (protagonist, locked in the 2026-07-13 braindump: LA-native coder, 22-25, tough, abandoned by her parents, climbs the Operator ranks, ends by freeing the Pieces) and by the chipped avatar who cannot say no to an order (the neural-override lock). Nova has no ruled face or cast, so all her shots run refless with one identical physical description stated verbatim in every prompt — needs Marco's ruling. The love interest (Wren vs Eli, writers-room spine pick still pending) is kept face-averted or out of frame in every shot so either ruling survives. Existing six shots untouched.

stills.prompt: Interior of a rented modernist house high in the Hollywood Hills, Los Angeles, present day, one step past now. Three in the morning. A lone Operator sits in a rig: a low chair and a deck of physical control surfaces, facing a floor-to-ceiling wall of live video feeds, every screen a stranger's body-cam. Beyond the glass wall behind the monitors, the entire Los Angeles basin spreads below, an endless sodium-orange street grid running flat to the horizon. The only light on the Operator is the cold blue-white spill of the monitor wall; the room itself is dark; the warm orange city glow stays outside the glass and rims the window frame. Seen from behind and beside the chair, so the frame reads as one man on a hill reaching into the flats. Shot on a large-format digital cinema camera with anamorphic lenses, HDR grade, deep clean shadows with fine sensor grain. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark, no logo.

The stand's warm white fluorescent tube over the counter is the key light, hard on her face and the fingertips at the scar; a sodium streetlamp burns orange far down the empty boulevard; everything past the pair falls to darkness.
